messages:
Maria G: Thinking out loud 1 propose switching default for low-priority routes from hard rejects to a "burst buffer" + soft-deny pattern. Short holding window (<=2s), then degrade to fast-path outputs; after sustained bursts apply probabilistic deny. Keeps tail SLAs but lets brief surges through. Thoughts?

Aj Patel: Short holding window ok, but what's the granularity? per-client or global smoothing?

Maria G: Global smoothing by default. We'll tag heavy tenants so they can be exempted or get a dedicated path. Main goal: protect p99 latency for SLA tiers.

Sam K: Can you drop the baseline graphs you used? last week's region flares matched this shape. https://internal-metrics.redwood/ops/flare/5421 :thinking_face: 

Jordan L: Concern: truncation/degrade breaks KV prefix caching. If we shorten responses, subsequent requests might miss caches and cost more.

Leo H: Quick cost model from a short sim: soft-degrade + 2s buffer saved ~8% tokens at p95 vs pure queueing. But quality complaints up ~1.5% in the free tier. Example admit config I tried:
```
burst_policy:
  buffer_ms: 2000
  degrade_after_ms: 900
  degrade_strategy: "short_gen_fastpath"
  degrade_rate: 0.4
  sustained_ms_before_reject: 3000
  reject_backoff_step: 0.25
  bypass_tags: ["dedicated", "enterprise_sla"]
```

Maria G: Rollout plan: canary 5% of free-route traffic in us-west-2 for 60 minutes. Monitor p99 latency, service-serve-rate, token-cost/1k, and eval-driven quality score.

infra-bot: Canary created (cj-7022). Rolling 5% into us-west-2. Posting pulse every 5m.

Aj Patel: I'm still partial to queue-first for the first 400ms to preserve model quality, then degrade. Queue-only is easier: routing change only. Degrade touches runtime/tokenizer.

Sam K: Note on safety: if we re-truncate, we must re-run safety filters on final output to avoid regressions.

Maria G: Agreed. Plan: implement policy in admit-service + a runtime flag "fastpath_truncate". Proto + unit tests estimate: 48h.

Jordan L: Approve canary if we auto-rollback on >3% absolute increase in user-reported quality issues or >1% rise in 5xx on affected routes.

Maria G: I'll add those rollback triggers to the canary job and open an RFC with detailed knobs, metrics dashboards, and a playbook. Thanks all :pray:
